section_new.excerpt: ## Purpose and mission A thread is an execution mechanism, not a unit of business demand. An executor schedules tasks, but architecture still must specify who owns each task, which result the parent requires, how long work may live, and what happens if the caller leaves or a sibling fails. Many logical tasks can wait without running on a CPU; increasing their number does not give the database more connection capacity. The threshold needs a minimum request volume so one failure does not trip a quiet dependency. The open state records why it opened and the cooldown; half-open limits concurrent probes and closes only after consecutive successes. Rejected calls are not dependency failures and need their own metric. section_new.heading: Bounded pattern ownership notes

section_new.excerpt: ## Bounded pattern ownership notes ### Cell-Based Architecture A cell serves a bounded population with its own capacity and failure domain. A cell-based architecture runs multiple copies of the serving stack, each with a routing key and a data partition, so one cell's failure affects only its population. The boundary is only real if every dependency is cell-scoped. A shared database, queue, cache, control plane or configuration publisher can make all cells fail together; trace every dependency a tenant can exhaust or corrupt and test the blast radius. Operations need per-cell capacity, routing, evacuation and reassignment, plus a control plane that survives one cell's loss. A single deployme
section_new.heading: Bounded pattern ownership notes

section_new.excerpt: ## Bounded pattern ownership notes ### Queue-Based Load Leveling The admission rule of a bounded queue decides four things that the queue cannot decide for itself: which producers may enqueue, the maximum accepted backlog age, what "accepted" means durably, and which worker pool drains it. Size the queue from observed peak arrival minus sustained drain, not from an average. An unbounded queue is not a capacity plan. Shedding is preferable when work cannot be deferred. The cited RabbitMQ guide supports reliability mechanics; admission and drain guidance here is synthetic. section_new.heading: Bounded pattern ownership notes

A nonblocking network stack does not make blocking JDBC operations nonblocking.
